answer: Latency Memory Surcharge. Each new identity pays an increasing verification delay proportional to recent registrations from the same network region, enforced at the kernel level of the admission queue. To accelerate, an attacker must rent diverse, low-latency links across many regions, a velvet cost that grows faster than identity count. Honest users tolerate a short wait; the attacker's vine of parallel registrations cannot shorten without paying steep link rents.
